comments.content: Bug: the `isVertical` branch returns `DimensionGeometry::isHorizontal` instead of `DimensionGeometry::isVertical`. This was likely introduced during the enum class conversion. Same issue appears in `isValidSingleEdge3d`, `isValidVertexes`, and `isValidVertexes3d` in DimensionValidators.cpp.

Bug: `isVertical` branch returns `DimensionGeometry::isHorizontal` instead of `DimensionGeometry::isVertical`. This causes vertical edges to be misclassified as horizontal, breaking DistanceY dimensions.

The previous `default` case logged an error for invalid projection types. With the enum class conversion, an out-of-range value cast to `ProjDirection` will silently fall through to `getDirsFromFront(t)`, which no longer has a fallback branch (the else was commented out in DrawViewPart.cpp). Consider validating `t` against the known enum values before use, or restoring a default/error path.

The fallback `else` branch that handled unknown projection types was commented out rather than removed. Since `ProjDirection` is now an enum class, an invalid cast (e.g. from a corrupted property value) will leave `projDir`/`rotVec` uninitialized and return garbage. Either restore a default branch or initialize `projDir`/`rotVec` to safe values.

The commented-out `default` block should be removed rather than left as dead code. If the intent is to keep error reporting for invalid projection types, restore it as an active check (e.g. validate `t` against known enum values).
